english.title: Carrier - vehicle carrying dangerous / pressurised goods fail to display an orange placard

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the carrier in relation to a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), being driven on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), by **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF THE DRIVER..) and failed to ensure that, when the vehicle was carrying goods or equipment subject to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHARACTER OF THE GOODS / EQUIPMENT..),

(A)_[in a container,]_
(B)_[in a multiple-element gas container,]_
(C)_[in an uncertified multiple-element gas container,]_
(D)_[in a tank-container,]_
(E)_[in a portable tank,]_
(F)_[in a demountable tank,]_
(G)_[which were packaged, the quantity being carried exceeded the total threshold for their transport category,]_
(H)_[in bulk,]_

it displayed placards and orange-coloured plates in accordance with paragraph 5 of Schedule 1 to those regulations
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 5 and 6 of and Schedule 1 to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 and section 33(1)(c) and (3) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For further guidance see the prosecution guide.
(ii) In the first instance a prohibition notice under section 22 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 should be considered subject to current HSE policy. Failure to comply with that prohibition should result in prosecution. Care should however be taken to obtain evidence to prove that the operator in the interim period had not complied with and therefore discharged the prohibition notice.
(iii) Where there is evidence of multiple offences, blatant disregard of the regulations or there has been previous advice, prosecution should also be considered.
(iv) The information specified in ADR 5.4 where relevant should form part of the transportation documents.
(v) The word "appropriate is open to interpretation
(vi) A prohibition notice is appropriate if the information is so lacking that the inspector is unable to identify what is being carried.
(vii) ADR 2009 section 5.3 refers.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: A fine.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
